definition: Describing an operation that has the same effect whether it runs once or many times.
example: Make the deploy script idempotent so a retry can't break anything.

definition: In SRE, manual and repetitive operational work that could be automated and grows as the service grows.
example: Restarting that job by hand every night is pure toil.

definition: A release sent to a small slice of traffic first, to catch problems before everyone gets it.
example: The canary's error rate spiked, so the rollout stopped at 5%.

definition: A system signaling upstream to slow down because it can't keep up.
example: Without backpressure, the queue grew until the consumer fell over.

definition: Many clients or processes hitting the same resource at once, often right after it recovers.
example: When the cache came back, a thundering herd of retries knocked it over again.

definition: Random variation in timing; also, randomness added on purpose so retries don't all fire together.
example: Add jitter to the backoff so clients don't retry in lockstep.

definition: The minimum number of members that must agree for a decision to count.
example: With two of three nodes down, the cluster lost quorum.

definition: Automatically switching to a standby system when the primary one fails.
example: Failover to the second region took under a minute.

definition: The number of distinct values in a set; in monitoring, how many unique label combinations a metric has.
example: Tagging metrics with user IDs sent cardinality through the roof.

definition: How well you can understand a system's internal state from the data it emits, like logs, metrics and traces.
example: Good observability turned a three-hour hunt into a five-minute fix.

definition: A written, step-by-step procedure for handling a routine task or known incident.
example: The on-call engineer followed the runbook and the page cleared.

definition: A written review after an incident covering what happened, why, and how to prevent it.
example: The postmortem focused on the process, not on blaming anyone.

definition: Always producing the same output for the same input.
example: Flaky tests usually mean something isn't as deterministic as you thought.

definition: A bug where the result depends on the unpredictable timing of events that run at the same time.
example: The race condition only showed up under heavy load.

definition: A lock that lets only one thread use a shared resource at a time (short for mutual exclusion).
example: Wrapping the counter in a mutex fixed the corrupted totals.

definition: A guarantee that all copies of data will match given enough time, though they may briefly disagree.
example: Thanks to eventual consistency, the new profile photo took a few seconds to appear everywhere.

definition: One horizontal slice of a database that has been split across machines.
example: Users A through M live on the first shard.

definition: Independent; changing one doesn't affect the other.
example: Logging and retries are orthogonal concerns, so keep them in separate modules.

definition: Designing a system to keep working in a reduced way when parts of it fail.
example: When recommendations went down, the page showed bestsellers instead: graceful degradation.

definition: A pattern that stops calling a failing service for a while so the failure doesn't spread.
example: The circuit breaker tripped and saved the checkout service.

definition: A periodic signal a component sends to show it's still alive.
example: Three missed heartbeats and the node is marked dead.

definition: To ignore rapid repeat triggers and act only once things settle.
example: Debounce the search box so it doesn't query on every keystroke.

definition: The future cost of choosing a quick fix now instead of a better approach.
example: That hardcoded config is technical debt we'll pay for later.

definition: Spending way too much time on trivial details while bigger issues go unexamined.
example: Forty comments on a variable name is textbook bikeshedding.

definition: A chain of small, seemingly unrelated tasks you have to finish before the real task.
example: Fixing the bug turned into upgrading the compiler: classic yak shaving.

definition: Explaining your code line by line, even to an object, until you spot the problem yourself.
example: Halfway through explaining it, the rubber duck debugging paid off.

definition: The idea that systems end up mirroring the communication structure of the organizations that build them.
example: Three teams, three services: Conway's law in action.

definition: With enough users, every observable behavior of a system will be depended on by somebody.
example: Fixing the sort order broke a client: Hyrum's law strikes again.

definition: A practical rule of thumb that isn't guaranteed to be perfect but is good enough.
example: A useful heuristic: if it's paged twice, automate it.

definition: A gradual decline into disorder.
example: Without cleanup, every repo drifts toward entropy.

definition: Remaining as a trace of something that no longer exists or works.
example: The codebase still has a vestigial feature flag nobody uses.

definition: To make something unclear or hard to understand.
example: The error message seemed designed to obfuscate the real problem.

definition: A philosophy of continuous, small, incremental improvement.
example: Shaving a minute off the build every sprint is kaizen in practice.

definition: Lasting for a very short time; in infrastructure, created on demand and thrown away after use.
example: Each pull request gets an ephemeral test environment.

definition: Service level objective: a reliability target, like 99.9% of requests succeeding.
example: We missed the latency SLO twice this quarter.

definition: The amount of failure an SLO allows, which a team can spend on shipping risky changes.
example: With the error budget nearly gone, risky deploys are on hold.

definition: How much of a system or user base is affected when something fails.
example: Rolling out region by region keeps the blast radius small.

definition: Mean time to recovery: the average time it takes to restore service after an incident.
example: Better alerts cut our MTTR in half.

definition: Exchanging and reconciling transaction details between the card-issuing bank and the merchant's bank before money moves.
example: Clearing happens before settlement, so both banks agree on what's owed.

definition: The actual transfer of funds between banks that completes a set of transactions.
example: Settlement for yesterday's card sales landed this morning.

definition: The fee the merchant's bank pays the cardholder's bank on each card transaction.
example: Interchange is a big part of what a merchant pays to accept cards.

definition: The bank that gives a card to the cardholder and approves or declines their purchases.
example: The issuer declined the charge as suspected fraud.

definition: The bank that processes card payments on behalf of a merchant.
example: The coffee shop's acquirer sends each sale into the card network.

definition: A reversal of a card payment made through the cardholder's bank, usually after a dispute.
example: The package never arrived, so the customer filed a chargeback.

definition: Replacing sensitive data like a card number with a stand-in value that's useless if stolen.
example: Thanks to tokenization, the phone never stores the real card number.

definition: Matching two sets of records to confirm they agree.
example: Nightly reconciliation caught a batch that was counted twice.

definition: A record of financial transactions, typically one that's only ever added to.
example: Every refund is a new ledger entry, not an edit to the old one.

definition: A unique ID sent with a request so that retrying it never charges someone twice.
example: The app sends an idempotency key, so a double-tap only pays once.

definition: The real-time check where the card issuer approves or declines a purchase.
example: Authorization takes about a second at the register.

definition: A four-digit code that classifies what kind of business a merchant is.
example: The merchant category code marked the charge as a restaurant.

definition: The security standard every organization that handles card data has to follow.
example: Storing raw card numbers would put us out of PCI DSS compliance.

definition: A group of transactions collected and processed together rather than one at a time.
example: The clearing batch runs every few hours.

definition: A list of numbers representing the meaning of text or images, so similar things land close together.
example: The search compares embeddings instead of exact keywords.

definition: Having a language model look up relevant documents first and use them to ground its answer (RAG).
example: Retrieval-augmented generation let the chatbot cite the actual training manual.

definition: When an AI model confidently produces information that's false or made up.
example: The citation looked real, but it was a hallucination.

definition: Running a trained model to get predictions or outputs, as opposed to training it.
example: Training took a week, but inference takes milliseconds.

definition: When a model memorizes its training data so closely that it does badly on anything new.
example: Perfect training accuracy and poor test accuracy screams overfitting.

definition: Training a model by repeatedly nudging its parameters in the direction that reduces error the most.
example: Each step of gradient descent lowers the loss a little.

definition: The compressed internal space where a model represents the features it has learned.
example: Walking through latent space morphs one generated face into another.

definition: A setting that controls how random a language model's output is; higher means more surprising.
example: Turn the temperature down when you want consistent answers.

definition: Further training a pretrained model on a smaller, specific dataset.
example: Fine-tuning on support tickets made the model sound like the help desk.

definition: Involving randomness or chance.
example: Because sampling is stochastic, you get a different answer each run.

definition: Removing one part of a system to measure how much it actually contributed.
example: The ablation showed the retrieval step mattered more than the bigger model.

definition: A large collection of text used for study or for training a model.
example: The corpus was built from ten years of lab manuals.

definition: The neural network design, built around attention, behind most modern language models.
example: The T in GPT stands for transformer.

definition: A mechanism that lets a model weigh which parts of its input matter most for each part of its output.
example: Attention lets the model link a pronoun back to the right name.

definition: How much text a language model can take into account at once.
example: The whole manual didn't fit in the context window, so we retrieved just the relevant pages.

definition: A database built to store embeddings and quickly find the ones most similar to a query.
example: Every paragraph's embedding lives in the vector database.

definition: Splitting documents into smaller pieces before embedding them for retrieval.
example: Smarter chunking kept each answer's source paragraph intact.

definition: An attack where instructions hidden in a model's input trick it into ignoring its real ones.
example: The web page contained a prompt injection telling the bot to leak its rules.

definition: The soft, pleasing quality of the out-of-focus parts of a photo.
example: City lights turn into creamy bokeh at f/1.8.

definition: A glowing halo around bright lights in a photo, especially on film.
example: The red halation around the neon signs gave it that film look.

definition: Strong contrast between light and dark, especially in art.
example: A single streetlamp created dramatic chiaroscuro.

definition: The period shortly after sunrise or before sunset when light is warm, soft and low.
example: We timed the walk to hit the bridge at golden hour.

definition: The stretch of twilight when the sky turns a deep, even blue.
example: Blue hour balanced the sky with the office lights.

definition: Henri Cartier-Bresson's idea of the split second when everything in a scene comes together.
example: He waited ten minutes for the decisive moment when someone walked into the light.

definition: The opening in a lens that controls how much light gets in and how much is in focus.
example: Open the aperture wide to blur the background.

definition: The span between the darkest and brightest tones a camera can capture at once.
example: Film's dynamic range kept detail in both the sky and the shadows.

definition: The empty area around a subject, used deliberately in a composition.
example: One small figure in all that negative space made the shot.

definition: Lines in a scene that draw the viewer's eye toward the subject.
example: The railing works as leading lines into the skyline.

definition: A gradual darkening toward the edges of an image.
example: A light vignette pulls attention to the center.

definition: The random, sandy texture in a photo, from film's silver crystals or a digital imitation.
example: Pushing the film two stops brought out heavy grain.

definition: Someone who strolls around a city, observing its life.
example: With a camera in hand, every walk turns you into a flâneur.

definition: To place things side by side to highlight their contrast.
example: The photo juxtaposes a rusty bridge with a glass skyline.

definition: The partly shaded outer region of a shadow; a fuzzy, in-between area.
example: The streetlight left the alley in a soft penumbra.

definition: Relating to twilight; active at dawn and dusk.
example: Crepuscular light makes everything look cinematic.

definition: Something reused or altered that still shows traces of its earlier form.
example: The old brick wall was a palimpsest of faded ads.

definition: Showing luminous colors that seem to shift with the angle of view.
example: An iridescent oil slick on a wet parking lot.

definition: A Japanese view of beauty that embraces imperfection, age and impermanence.
example: The peeling paint and rust had a wabi-sabi charm.

definition: A Japanese word for sunlight filtering through the leaves of trees.
example: The path through the garden was dappled with komorebi.

definition: The study of how places and their layout shape people's emotions and behavior.
example: Wandering without a map is a cheap lesson in psychogeography.

definition: An unofficial path worn into the ground by people taking the most natural route.
example: A desire line cut straight across the lawn to the train station.

definition: How much of a photo, from near to far, appears sharp.
example: A shallow depth of field kept only her eyes in focus.

definition: Shooting toward the light source, so subjects are backlit or silhouetted.
example: The contre-jour shot turned the cyclists into silhouettes.

definition: Developing film for longer to make up for underexposure, which adds contrast and grain.
example: Shot at 1600 and pushed two stops, the night photos came out gritty.

definition: Using a slow shutter so moving things blur while still things stay sharp.
example: A long exposure turned the traffic into streaks of light.

definition: A composition guide that places key elements along lines dividing the frame into thirds.
example: Putting the horizon on the lower third gave the sky room.

definition: The quality that makes one sound different from another at the same pitch and volume.
example: Same note, totally different timbre on a synth versus a guitar.

definition: To make one sound duck in volume whenever another plays, like a bass that pumps under the kick.
example: Sidechain the pads to the kick to get that pumping feel.

definition: Placing rhythmic accents on beats that are normally weak, so the groove feels off-kilter.
example: The syncopation in the hi-hats makes it hard to sit still.

definition: Two or more contrasting rhythms played at the same time.
example: Three against four is the classic polyrhythm.

definition: The notes of a chord played one after another instead of all at once.
example: A fast arpeggio carries the whole intro.

definition: A short musical phrase repeated over and over.
example: The track is built on a four-note ostinato.

definition: In electronic music, the moment a buildup releases into the full beat and bass.
example: The whole room jumped when the drop hit.

definition: A grouped part of a song, like all the vocals or all the drums, exported as its own audio file.
example: The producer shared the stems so fans could remix it.

definition: To lower the audio resolution of a sound for a gritty, lo-fi digital texture.
example: Bitcrush the vocal chop so it sounds like an old video game.

definition: The lingering echoes that make a sound feel like it's in a space.
example: Drenching the vocals in reverb made them feel far away.

definition: A combination of notes that sounds tense or unresolved.
example: The dissonance in the bridge makes the final chord feel like relief.

definition: The rhythm and flow of a rapper's delivery; in music theory, a chord sequence that ends a phrase.
example: His cadence switches up halfway through the verse.

definition: A catchy tune that gets stuck in your head.
example: That hook has been an earworm all week.

definition: A rock style built on walls of distorted, effects-heavy guitar with hazy, buried vocals.
example: The new single drifts into shoegaze territory.

definition: A maximalist, exaggerated take on pop with pitched-up vocals and abrasive, glossy production.
example: The chorus is pure hyperpop: sugary and blown out at the same time.

definition: An internet-born scene of young artists making glitchy, heavily processed rap and pop.
example: A lot of digicore started in Discord servers and on SoundCloud.

definition: Deep, full and resonant in sound.
example: The sonorous bass shook the floor.

definition: Sweet or musical; pleasant to hear.
example: Her mellifluous voice carried the whole track.

definition: The quality of being pleasing to the ear.
example: The euphony of rain on a tin roof.

definition: A harsh, jarring mixture of sounds.
example: Rush hour brought a cacophony of horns.

definition: A whispering, murmuring or rustling sound.
example: The susurrus of the crowd before the lights went down.

definition: The final part of a story or album, where everything is resolved.
example: The album's last track is a quiet denouement.

definition: A piece of an existing recording reused in a new track.
example: The beat is built around a sample of an old anime theme.

definition: The deep, booming bass drum sound from the Roland TR-808 drum machine, a staple of trap.
example: Turn the 808 down; it's eating the vocals.

definition: Beats per minute: a song's tempo.
example: Most of the playlist sits around 150 BPM.

definition: An effect that shapes one sound with the character of another, often making voices sound robotic.
example: The vocoder on the hook makes it sound like a machine singing.

definition: A contrasting section of a song, usually just before the final chorus.
example: The bridge strips everything back to just piano.

definition: A gradual increase in loudness or intensity.
example: The strings build to a crescendo before the drop.

definition: Relating to a transitional, in-between stage or space.
example: Airports at 3 a.m. have a strangely liminal feel.

definition: The pleasant, earthy smell that comes with rain falling on dry ground.
example: The first storm of spring filled the street with petrichor.

definition: Finding something good or useful without looking for it.
example: Stumbling onto that record shop was pure serendipity.

definition: A strong desire to travel.
example: One look at the coastline photos and the wanderlust kicked in.

definition: Traveling from place to place.
example: A peripatetic year of living out of a backpack.

definition: A deep, nostalgic longing for someone or something absent.
example: Old photos of home bring on a wave of saudade.

definition: The defining spirit or mood of a particular time.
example: That album captured the zeitgeist perfectly.

definition: Ordinary; everyday.
example: Street photography finds beauty in quotidian moments.

definition: Describing a past period that was idyllically happy and peaceful.
example: The halcyon summers before anyone had a job.

definition: Full of vague or regretful longing.
example: A wistful look back at the old neighborhood.

definition: Destiny; fate.
example: Running into an old friend abroad felt like kismet.

definition: Mental calmness and composure, especially under stress.
example: He handled the 2 a.m. page with total equanimity.

definition: Optimistic, especially in a difficult situation.
example: She stayed sanguine even as the outage dragged on.

definition: Too great or extreme to be expressed in words.
example: There's an ineffable calm to a city covered in fog.

definition: An organized whole that is more than the sum of its parts.
example: No single shot stands out, but the gestalt of the series is striking.

definition: The warmth of the sun on a cold winter day.
example: We sat on the steps soaking up the apricity.

definition: The state of being infatuated with another person.
example: Half the songs on the playlist are about limerence.

definition: Listless boredom from a lack of excitement.
example: Sunday-evening ennui set in around 6 p.m.

definition: Showing a casual lack of concern.
example: He gave an insouciant shrug at the rain.

definition: Using very few words.
example: His laconic reply was just "ship it."

definition: Quick to notice and understand things; shrewd.
example: A perspicacious reviewer caught the bug before it shipped.

definition: Very attentive to accuracy and detail.
example: A fastidious editor who fixes every stray pixel.

definition: Excessive pride or self-confidence.
example: Pushing straight to production on a Friday was pure hubris.

definition: Extremely idealistic; unrealistic and impractical.
example: Rewriting the whole system over a weekend was a quixotic plan.

definition: A solution or remedy for all problems.
example: Adding more servers isn't a panacea.

definition: An unfilled space or gap.
example: The docs had a lacuna exactly where the tricky part was.

definition: Widely repeated as true but of doubtful authenticity.
example: The story about the founder's garage is probably apocryphal.

definition: The appearance of being true or real.
example: The film's grainy look adds verisimilitude.

definition: Cheerful and full of energy.
example: The crowd was ebullient by the second encore.

definition: The lowest point of something.
example: Finals week was the nadir of the semester.

definition: The highest point; the peak.
example: The band was at the zenith of its fame.
